previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A female patient with end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis, systemic lupus erythematosus, and antiphospholipid syndrome was readmitted due to nausea and abdominal pain that began on the day of discharge from a prior admission for posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES). Evaluation revealed mild tenderness around the peritoneal dialysis catheter site, prompting concern for catheter-related infection or inflammation. Imaging ruled out bowel perforation and abscess, and dialysis fluid studies showed no infection. Blood and stool cultures were negative. A central venous catheter was placed for dialysis access due to internal jugular vein thrombosis and elevated INR. MRI confirmed resolution of prior PRES. The patient improved with antibiotics and supportive care, and was discharged when symptoms resolved and stability was achieved.

Because of her history of bleeding disorder ___ deficiency)
